_comment: THE cross-language color contract. Go, TypeScript and elisp each assert
their own table against this file, row for row, which is the only
mechanism that makes a divergence between the three fail loudly instead
of quietly.
It pins WHICH of the six colors a state takes AND what each color's
value is ('color_values'): a status is one color on every surface, the
Emacs tab bar's fill and the webapp's dot alike (owner ruling,
2026-10-17). A workspace that reads green in one surface and red in
another, or a green tab beside a different green dot, is the failure
this file exists to prevent.
'none' is a real answer, not a gap. The merge states deliberately carry
glyphs instead of colors so they never spend one of the five, and a
workspace with no session has no lifecycle verdict to paint. A surface
may override 'none' per state — see 'surface_overrides' — but only by
DECLARING the override here.
WHAT EACH COLOR MEANS (owner ruling, 2026-09-28; restated in
modules/app/agent-repl/AGENTS.md, 'What each status color means'):
red        the agent is working: a turn is submitting, thinking,
taking on context, clearing or compacting. Usable.
yellow     the main thread is idle while detached work runs. Usable.
green      ready for the user: idle, a turn done or interrupted, a
permission, question or cold gate standing (owner ruling,
2026-10-08: the same green as done), a merge that landed or
failed (owner ruling, 2026-10-13: the workspace is ready to
be looked at; the glyph's red ink says what there is to see).
Usable.
purple     a merge is IN PROGRESS; the daemon holds the workspace, so
the composer is closed.
turquoise  something unexpected went wrong and wants the user's
attention, but the workspace is USABLE: a failed turn, a
degraded view of a serving session, or a VENDOR FAULT (the
vendor will not start, a vendor or account block, a call the
vendor is retrying) -- prompts are held until the vendor
serves.
blue       the workspace is UNUSABLE right now: an AGENT-REPL FAULT
(a severed or dead route, a failed start, an impaired
daemon), a NETWORK FAULT (this machine is offline), or a
close under way.
none       GREY: nothing is wrong and nothing runs -- a workspace
incidentally inactive (closed, or being opened) and a session
booting (owner ruling, 2026-10-13: booting is an expected
step, never a fault).
THE FAULT DOMAINS (owner ruling, 2026-10-02): agent_repl_fault and
network_fault are blue, vendor_fault is turquoise, with the precedence
agent_repl_fault > network_fault > vendor_fault.
THE COMPOSER INVARIANT: a composer is closed exactly when its footer's
status color is one of 'composer_closed_colors' (blue). A
renderer derives its gate from this file, never from a list of arms.
Whether a status draws FULL (unread) or PARTIAL (viewed) is independent
of its color, and nothing here speaks to it.
STATES ARE NAMED BY THEIR frontend.v1 ONEOF ARMS, not by a RENDER_STATE
enum. The daemon resolves every view, so the arm the daemon sets IS the
state a renderer paints, and there is no second spelling to keep aligned
by hand.
_color_values_comment: THE ONE VALUE OF EACH COLOR, per theme. Every renderer paints a color
from here and holds no hex of its own: the webapp defines its status
tokens from it (src/vocab.ts), and the Emacs tab bar, which is always
dark, fills its tabs with the 'dark' row (lisp/status.el).
The 'dark' row is the pastel set (owner ruling, 2026-10-17): each hue
kept, drawn at one lightness with its strength capped, red the deeper
red the webapp's cleared rule shares, purple the tool title's purple.
design-dark-accent-tuner.html beside this module derives it. The
dark green is the deeper #1a7a1a the tab bar's names wore (owner
ruling, 2026-10-17: the pastel green read light yet weak), then taken
0.06 lighter in OKLCH lightness to #318c2f (owner ruling, 2026-10-18;
design-green-lighter.html beside this module). The 'light'
row is the light theme's set as it stood. The dark red and blue are the
pastel ones taken 0.12 darker in OKLCH lightness, hue and strength kept
(owner ruling, 2026-10-18; design-red-blue-darker.html beside this
module). Then EVERY dark color was taken 0.12 darker in OKLCH
lightness with its chroma times 1.05, hue kept, chroma lowered only
to stay in gamut (owner rulings, 2026-10-28: the custom option of
design-darker-accents.html, its step then eased from 0.19 to 0.10,
then to 0.12); the webapp's dark accents took the same step.
A glyph-only ink with one drawn value is here too: 'orange', the
compaction orange a compacting turn's dot is inked with and the feed's
compacted rule is drawn in, one value on every surface (owner ruling,
2026-10-18: the dark one taken stronger, #ffc07a -> #ff9646;
design-compact-orange.html beside this module). 'amber' has no value:
the webapp, its one surface, draws it in the paused-queue amber its
merge bubbles are framed in (--merge-paused).
_precedence_comment: The six-color precedence, strongest claim first. Each color is a
strictly stronger claim about what the user CANNOT do, or must look at,
than the one beneath it, so the strongest true claim wins.
Blue leads because an unusable workspace denies everything else; purple
is the daemon holding the workspace for a merge; red is the agent holding
the turn; turquoise is a fault the user should look at while still able
to work; yellow is detached work the user can talk over; green is the
_roster_status_comment: Keyed by the RosterRow.status oneof arm names in
frontend/v1/sidebar.proto, spelled EXACTLY as the proto spells them.
A consumer asserts this map row for row against the proto's arm set:
every arm must appear here and every key here must be an arm, so a new
arm landing without a color fails the assertion instead of drawing an
unpainted dot.
EVERY MERGE ARM SPENDS A COLOR AS WELL AS A GLYPH: a merge in progress
(merge_queued, merging) is PURPLE, a landed merge (merged) and a failed
one (merge_failed) are GREEN, the workspace is back with the user and
ready to be looked at (owner ruling, 2026-10-13). A failed merge's
GLYPH is inked red ('glyph_inks'). A merge never parks and no merge fact
is shown before the requesting turn ends (merge-landing.md, Landed
change 1), so there is no conflict arm and no enqueuing arm, and a merge
waiting to start is merge_queued (owner ruling, 2026-10-13).
'none' and 'inactive' take 'none', drawn GREY: no session was ever
created, or the workspace is incidentally inactive (no open
perspective, or being opened, which the row's opening marker says).
'init' takes 'none' as well: a booting session is an expected step,
never a fault, and draws the same grey mark (owner ruling, 2026-10-13).
'turn_failed' and 'degraded' are TURQUOISE: something went wrong, but
the workspace is usable. 'severed', 'dead', 'start_failed' and
'turn_died' (the last turn died with agent-repl's own machinery, owner
ruling 2026-10-06) and 'daemon_impaired' (the daemon itself cannot
serve) are BLUE agent-repl faults, 'closing' (a refused close) is BLUE,
and 'network_fault' is a BLUE network fault: the workspace cannot be
used until the route or the network comes back. 'vendor_fault',
'vendor_blocked' and 'api_retrying' are TURQUOISE vendor faults: the
workspace stays usable and a prompt is held until the vendor serves
(owner ruling, 2026-10-02). 'permission', 'question' and 'cold_gate' (a
gate waits on the user) are GREEN, the same green as 'done' (owner
ruling, 2026-10-08), and so is 'waiting' (an interrupt landing). Every
roster arm takes the color of the footer status it projects. An async
merge of the workspace's own branch is no arm: it is the row's
RosterRowAsyncMerging marker, drawn per 'async_merge_mark'.

merge arm does (owner rulings, 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-13); a merge arm
painted without being declared here is refused, so a new merge arm must
_merge_glyphs_comment: GLYPH NAMES, not characters. Each renderer maps these names to whatever
its surface can actually draw -- a webapp icon, an Emacs character.
What is shared is WHICH glyph a merge state gets, never the character.
EVERY MERGE ARM DRAWS THE ONE 'merge' GLYPH (owner ruling, 2026-10-13):
its ink says which arm it is (the arm's color, or its 'glyph_inks' row)
and 'merging' breathes, as every animated mark does.
Keyed by the merge arms of RosterRow.status. 'feed_merge_head_glyph' is
separate because it names FeedMergeGlyph.icon on the feed's merge
bubble head, which reports the merge as a whole rather than one of its

AND draws a glyph in place of the plain status mark, so the user can

_glyph_inks_comment: THE GLYPH'S INK, where it differs from the arm's color (owner ruling,
2026-10-13). The arm's color is the WORKSPACE's status and stays what
'roster_status' says -- the Emacs tab's background, the sidebar row's
name -- while the mark drawn beside the name takes this ink: a failed
merge is a green workspace whose merge glyph is red, and a compacting
turn is a red workspace whose dot is the orange of the feed's
compaction rule. An arm absent here inks its mark in its own color.
An ink is one of the six colors or one of 'glyph_only_colors', which no
status may take: each renderer keeps its own value for them as it does
_async_merge_mark_comment: 2026-10-13): the workspace's own branch merges async in a hidden merge
workspace while the workspace stays free. The row's status arm, and so
its NAME's color in the sidebar and its NAME's background on the Emacs
tab, is the workspace's own status throughout. Only the mark changes:
sidebar  the row's PLAIN status dot -- glyph 'dot' with no
'glyph_inks' row and no one-shot glyph standing -- is drawn
as 'glyph', a 'merge_glyphs' name (the merge arms' three
bars, owner request 2026-10-14), in 'ink' and 'motion' in
place of the arm's own. Every other mark outranks it: a
gate's glyph, the one-shot glyph, a merge glyph, an inked dot
(compacting's orange) and no mark at all.
tab bar  the tab's '[N]' bracket takes 'tab_bracket' as its
background; the space after it and the name keep the
status background. No glyph is drawn.
A SYNC merge raises no mark: it is the row's own merge arms.
_paused_merge_mark_comment: 2026-10-14): the merge queue holding the row's merge is paused, so the
merge is not progressing. The sidebar draws every merge indicator of
the row -- the merge glyph of a 'merging' or 'merge_queued' row, and the
'async_merge_mark' -- in 'ink' instead of its own, and the breath the
merge gave the row's name takes 'motion'. The row's status color, and so
its name's color, is untouched, and a breath the row's own status arm
draws (a turn in flight) stands. The tab bar draws nothing for it.
The ink is the amber a paused queue's merge bubble is framed in, so
the sidebar and the feed say 'paused' in one color (owner request,
_one_shot_glyph_arms_comment: THE ONE-SHOT GLYPH (frontend.v1.RosterRowOneShot) is drawn in place of
the status mark ONLY while the one-shot works: on these arms and no
other (owner ruling, 2026-10-13). Every other arm, compacting included,
draws its own mark. The glyph is static.
_footer_status_comment: Keyed by the FooterStatus.status oneof arm names in
frontend/v1/footer.proto. Every footer arm makes the same coarse claim
as the roster arm of the same meaning (resolve/ladder), and takes the
same color.
BLUE is 'agent_repl_fault', 'network_fault' and 'closing': the workspace
cannot be used, so the composer is closed.
TURQUOISE 'vendor_fault' is the vendor or the account refusing the
session (a vendor start retried, rejected or given up on, a usage limit,
auth, billing, a call being retried): the workspace is usable, the
composer stays open and a prompt is held until the vendor serves.
PURPLE is 'merging', a merge in flight; the composer is closed.
TURQUOISE is 'turn_failed' and 'degraded' (owner ruling, 2026-09-28):
something went wrong, but the workspace is usable and the composer is
open.
GREY 'starting' is the session booting (owner ruling, 2026-10-13): an
expected step, never a fault, so the composer stays open and a prompt
is held until the session is up.
GREEN 'merged' is a merge that landed, and 'merge_failed' one that
failed: either way the workspace is back with the user (owner ruling,
GREEN 'permission' and 'question' are a gate standing on the user (owner
ruling, 2026-10-08): the same green as 'idle', never a working red.
_composer_closed_colors_comment: THE COMPOSER INVARIANT (owner ruling, 2026-09-28): a composer is
CLOSED exactly when its footer status arm's color (footer_status) is
one of these, and open otherwise. Blue is an unusable workspace; every
other color is a usable one. Purple, a merge in flight, left this list
on 2026-10-01 (owner ruling): a prompt submitted during a merge is held
until the merge ends, so the composer stays open.
Renderers derive the gate from this list, never from arm names.
_composer_open_substatuses_comment: The DECLARED exceptions to the composer invariant, keyed by footer
status arm then listing that arm's substatus arms (spelled as the proto
spells them) whose composer stays OPEN although the status's color
closes it. 'agent_repl_fault · turn_died' is the one declared today
(owner ruling, 2026-10-06): the last turn died with agent-repl's own
machinery, the fault stands until the next turn starts, and a closed
composer would leave nothing to start it with. An exception is only
ever declared here; a renderer never opens a closed color on its own.
_topbar_connectivity_comment: TopbarConnectivity.tone, keyed by the daemon's link states. The topbar
reports the route to the session's shim, so its whole range is green
(serving), blue (the route is compromised) and 'none' (there is no
session to have a route to).
topbar.proto's comment on the `tone` field still lists teal. THE
COMMENT IS STALE and this file is authoritative: teal is not a value
any producer may emit, and 'topbar_tones' is the closed set a consumer
_surface_overrides_comment: A surface may paint a state differently from the shared assignment
above, but ONLY by naming the divergence here. Undeclared drift is
exactly what this file exists to prevent, so the escape hatch is a
declaration rather than a silent local table: a reader of any one
renderer still learns from this file that the surfaces disagree, and
each renderer asserts its own overrides against this section row for
row. A surface absent from this map takes 'roster_status' verbatim.
NO SURFACE OVERRIDES ANYTHING TODAY. The Emacs tab bar once painted the
in-flight merge arms purple over a shared 'none'; the shared table now
paints them purple itself (owner ruling, 2026-09-28), so every surface
_failure_sides_comment: The SIDES of a failure — failure.proto's own vocabulary, which replaced
the old error classes. A failure card takes the color of the side it
lands on: card color IS state color, from this one table, so a user
cannot see a purple workspace explained by a blue card.
machinery is agent-repl's own machinery being compromised and
client_local is the client's end of the same route; both are blue,
because both mean the route to a working session is broken and neither
is the vendor's doing. vendor is purple: the vendor or the account has
stopped the work, and nothing in agent-repl is wrong.
_feed_work_dots_comment: The dot leading a feed subagent bubble's head (frontend.v1.FeedSubagent)
and a detached shell bubble's head (frontend.v1.FeedShell), keyed by the
state arm: 'live', else the settled outcome arm. Owner request,
2026-10-01: running is a FILLED green dot, failed a FILLED red one, and a
run that settled successfully a HOLLOW one. A dot that spends no color
('none') is drawn hollow, every colored dot filled, so the shape needs no
cancelled is 'none' (hollow): the user's own stop ended it, so nothing went
wrong and nothing wants a look. lost is 'turquoise' (filled): we stopped
being able to see the run, which is unexpected and wants the user's
attention, but it is not a proven failure, so it does not take failed's
red. A shell has no 'failed' arm: a nonzero exit is still 'completed'.
settling is 'none' (hollow): the run stopped and its outcome is on its
way, so nothing wants a look yet. restarted is 'blue', with lost: the
vendor process restarted under the run, which neither the user nor the
